lessons.title: What Is T-SQL? A Tour of SSMS
Connecting to a Database & the USE Statement

slots.practicalActivity: In SSMS, connect to the local SQL Server instance, run USE AdventureWorks2012;, and expand Object Explorer's Tables node to find at least 8 real table names across the Person, Sales, and Production schemas. Write and run 3 SELECT TOP 10 * FROM queries against three different tables you found.
slots.deliverable: A saved .sql script with 3 working SELECT TOP 10 * FROM queries against three different AdventureWorks2012 tables, each with a one-line comment noting its schema.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 5 original SELECT queries against AdventureWorks2012: 2 using SELECT * and 3 selecting specific named columns (at least 3 columns each) from Person.Person, Production.Product, and Sales.SalesOrderHeader.
slots.deliverable: A .sql file with 5 working SELECT queries, each run successfully in SSMS with visible results.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 4 queries against Person.Person that alias at least 2 columns each with AS, and build a FullName column by concatenating FirstName + ' ' + LastName (handling a NULL MiddleName with ISNULL).
slots.deliverable: 4 queries with readable aliased column headers, including one FullName concatenation query.

slots.practicalActivity: Against Production.Product, write one simple CASE expression translating Color into a friendlier label (e.g. 'N/A' for NULL), and one searched CASE expression bucketing ListPrice into 'Budget', 'Mid-range', and 'Premium' using comparison ranges.
slots.deliverable: 2 queries with working CASE expressions, each producing a new derived column in the result set.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 SELECT DISTINCT queries against Sales.SalesOrderHeader and Person.Person (distinct TerritoryID, distinct City), then reformat 3 earlier queries from this chapter with consistent capitalization, indentation, and a header comment block.
slots.deliverable: 3 DISTINCT queries plus a cleaned-up, commented version of at least 3 earlier queries from this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for T-SQL Foundations: write one original query against AdventureWorks2012 that selects aliased columns from Person.Person, concatenates a full name, adds a CASE-based price-tier label joined from Production.Product, and applies DISTINCT — all in one commented statement.
slots.deliverable: One well-commented original query combining column aliasing, string concatenation, CASE, and DISTINCT.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 5 WHERE-clause queries against Sales.SalesOrderHeader and Production.Product using comparison operators (=, <>, >, <, >=, <=) to filter on OrderDate, TotalDue, and ListPrice.
slots.deliverable: 5 filtered queries, each returning a different row subset, with the row count noted in a comment.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 queries combining AND/OR/NOT against Production.Product (e.g. red OR blue AND under $500), then write 3 LIKE queries using %, _, and NOT LIKE against Person.Person.LastName.
slots.deliverable: 6 queries demonstrating compound boolean filters and wildcard pattern matches.

lessons.title: Handling NULL (IS NULL / IS NOT NULL)

slots.practicalActivity: Write 2 IN queries and 2 BETWEEN queries against Sales.SalesOrderHeader (specific TerritoryIDs, OrderDate ranges), then 2 IS NULL / IS NOT NULL queries against Person.Person.MiddleName and Production.Product.Color.
slots.deliverable: 6 queries covering IN, BETWEEN, and NULL-safe filtering, each verified in SSMS.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 ORDER BY queries (ascending, descending, multi-column) against Sales.SalesOrderHeader, then 2 TOP queries (TOP N and TOP N PERCENT) finding the highest-value orders.
slots.deliverable: 5 queries demonstrating sorting and TOP/TOP PERCENT limiting on real order data.

lessons.title: Predicates: How SQL Server Filters Data

slots.practicalActivity: Write a TOP WITH TIES query ordered by Production.Product.ListPrice to catch tied values, then write 2 queries comparing predicate evaluation on an indexed vs. non-indexed column using SET STATISTICS IO ON.
slots.deliverable: A TOP WITH TIES query returning tied rows, plus 2 predicate-comparison queries with STATISTICS IO output captured.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Filtering and Sorting: write one combined query against Sales.SalesOrderHeader that filters with a compound WHERE (AND/OR/IN/BETWEEN), handles NULLs safely, sorts the result, and returns only the TOP 10 WITH TIES, simulating a 'top customers by order value' report.
slots.deliverable: One original multi-clause query combining filtering, NULL handling, sorting, and TOP WITH TIES, with a comment explaining the business question it answers.

slots.practicalActivity: Use Object Explorer's Keys folders to identify the primary/foreign keys linking Sales.SalesOrderHeader to Sales.Customer and Person.Person, then write 2 INNER JOIN queries returning customer names with their order totals.
slots.deliverable: 2 INNER JOIN queries returning combined customer-and-order data, plus a note identifying the PK/FK pair used in each.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a LEFT JOIN from Production.Product to Sales.SalesOrderDetail to find products never ordered (NULL on the right side), then rewrite it as a RIGHT JOIN with the table order swapped and confirm the same result.
slots.deliverable: A LEFT JOIN query listing never-ordered products, plus an equivalent RIGHT JOIN proving the same result from the opposite table order.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a FULL OUTER JOIN between two related AdventureWorks2012 tables to surface unmatched rows on both sides, then a CROSS JOIN between distinct Production.Product.Color values and Production.ProductSubcategory, calculating the expected row count first.
slots.deliverable: A FULL OUTER JOIN showing unmatched rows, and a CROSS JOIN whose actual row count matches your pre-calculated estimate.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a SELF JOIN against Sales.SalesPerson's territory/manager structure to pair related rows, then a 3-table JOIN chaining Sales.SalesOrderHeader, Sales.SalesOrderDetail, and Production.Product to list order line items with real product names.
slots.deliverable: A working SELF JOIN query and a 3-table JOIN query returning order line items with real product names.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a CROSS APPLY that returns each Sales.Customer's top 3 highest-value orders from Sales.SalesOrderHeader via a correlated TOP subquery, then convert it to OUTER APPLY and compare which zero-order customers now appear.
slots.deliverable: A CROSS APPLY top-3-orders-per-customer query and its OUTER APPLY variant, with a one-line row-count comparison.

slots.practicalActivity: For 4 business questions you write yourself (e.g. 'all products and whether they've sold', 'every order with customer info'), decide which join type fits each and write the query, annotating each with a comment justifying the choice.
slots.deliverable: 4 queries, each preceded by a comment explaining why that join type was the right choice for the question.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one consolidated report query: INNER JOIN Sales.SalesOrderHeader to Sales.Customer and Person.Person for names, LEFT JOIN to Sales.SalesOrderDetail and Production.Product so orders with no line items still appear, ordered by OrderDate descending.
slots.deliverable: One multi-join report query mixing INNER and LEFT JOIN across at least 4 tables, producing a readable order-detail report.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Joining Tables: without looking back at lesson examples, write an original 5-table join query from scratch (SalesOrderHeader, SalesOrderDetail, Product, Customer, Person) listing each order's customer full name, product name, quantity, and line total, deliberately choosing INNER vs. LEFT JOIN for each relationship and documenting the choice in comments.
slots.deliverable: One original 5-table join lab query with full comments justifying each join type, executed successfully in SSMS.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 2 COUNT queries (COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT column)) against Sales.SalesOrderDetail, and 2 SUM/AVG queries computing the total and average LineTotal.
slots.deliverable: 4 aggregate queries returning single summary numbers from real order-detail data.

slots.practicalActivity: Write MIN/MAX queries finding the cheapest and most expensive product in Production.Product, then 3 single-column GROUP BY queries: total sales per ProductID, order count per CustomerID, average price per ProductSubcategoryID.
slots.deliverable: 2 MIN/MAX queries and 3 single-column GROUP BY aggregate queries.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a GROUP BY grouping Sales.SalesOrderDetail by ProductID and SpecialOfferID, then 2 queries contrasting HAVING (filtering the aggregate, e.g. total quantity sold > 500) vs. WHERE (filtering rows before aggregation) on the same data.
slots.deliverable: A multi-column GROUP BY query plus a side-by-side WHERE-vs-HAVING comparison on the same aggregate.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a UNION combining two differently-filtered SELECTs from Sales.SalesOrderHeader (big vs. small orders) and the same as UNION ALL, comparing row counts and duplicate handling; then write a VAR/STDEV query on TotalDue.
slots.deliverable: A UNION and UNION ALL pair showing the duplicate-removal difference, plus one VAR/STDEV statistical query.

slots.practicalActivity: Build an original summary-report query combining GROUP BY, HAVING, and at least 2 aggregate functions to answer: 'which product subcategories had total sales over a threshold you choose, ranked by total descending?'
slots.deliverable: One polished summary-report query with GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY producing a ranked business report.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Grouping and Aggregating: write an original sales-summary report joining Sales.SalesOrderHeader to Sales.SalesOrderDetail and Production.Product, grouping by product category, using COUNT/SUM/AVG together, filtering groups with HAVING, and sorting the final report.
slots.deliverable: One original multi-table aggregate report query combining joins, GROUP BY, HAVING, and multiple aggregate functions.

slots.practicalActivity: Inspect Person.Person and Production.ProductDescription column data types via sys.columns, noting which use CHAR, VARCHAR, and NVARCHAR; write 2 queries returning DATALENGTH() of a name column to compare storage.
slots.deliverable: 2 queries showing DATALENGTH results for real columns, plus written notes on which columns use each data type.

slots.practicalActivity: Find a VARCHAR(MAX) column in AdventureWorks2012 (e.g. Production.ProductReview.Comments) and query its LEN() against a handful of rows; then write 2 queries using LEN, UPPER, and LOWER on Person.Person.LastName.
slots.deliverable: A VARCHAR(MAX) LEN() query plus 2 LEN/UPPER/LOWER queries on real name data.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a SUBSTRING/CHARINDEX query that dynamically extracts a segment of a Production.Product.ProductNumber code by locating its '-' separator, then write a STUFF query masking part of a value and a REPLACE query swapping a character in Production.Product.Name.
slots.deliverable: One CHARINDEX-driven dynamic substring query, plus a STUFF vs. REPLACE comparison pair.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 TRIM/LTRIM/RTRIM queries cleaning whitespace from a concatenated name column, proving the before/after difference with LEN(); then query sys.columns to find 3 date/time columns in Sales.SalesOrderHeader and note their exact data types.
slots.deliverable: 3 trimming queries with LEN()-verified before/after proof, plus a written list of 3 real date/time columns and their types.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 GETDATE/DATEADD/DATEDIFF queries computing order age in days, a projected ship date, and orders placed in the last 30 days relative to the dataset's latest OrderDate; then write 2 CAST/CONVERT queries reformatting OrderDate into different string styles.
slots.deliverable: 3 date-function queries including a DATEDIFF-based 'days since order' calculation, plus 2 CAST/CONVERT formatting queries.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a scratch temp table with intentionally duplicated rows copied from Production.Product, then write a dedup query using ROW_NUMBER() to identify and delete the duplicates, verifying the before/after row count.
slots.deliverable: One working duplicate-removal query tested against a table with real duplicate rows, with before/after row counts noted.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Data Types, Strings, and Dates: build one combined data-cleaning query pulling Person.Person names, trimming whitespace, upper-casing the last name, concatenating a formatted full name, converting a date column to 'yyyy-mm-dd' string format, and using SUBSTRING to pull part of a phone number.
slots.deliverable: One combined string/date-cleaning query exercising at least 5 different functions from this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Data Types, Strings, and Dates: pick 3 columns across AdventureWorks2012 (one string, one date, one wide VARCHAR(MAX)) and write a one-paragraph design note explaining why each was likely given that specific data type.
slots.deliverable: A short written data-type justification note covering 3 real AdventureWorks2012 columns.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a scalar subquery finding all products priced above the average ListPrice, then a multi-value IN subquery finding orders placed by customers in a specific list of territories returned by a subquery against Sales.SalesTerritory.
slots.deliverable: A scalar-subquery 'above average price' query and a multi-value IN subquery query.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a correlated subquery returning each customer's most recent order date inline per row, then an EXISTS query finding customers with at least one order over $5,000 and a NOT EXISTS query finding products never ordered.
slots.deliverable: One correlated subquery and two EXISTS/NOT EXISTS queries, each verified against known AdventureWorks2012 data.

slots.practicalActivity: Rewrite one earlier subquery solution as a CTE for readability, then write a recursive CTE walking the Production.ProductCategory/ProductSubcategory hierarchy to list parent-child levels.
slots.deliverable: A readable CTE rewrite of a prior query, plus a working recursive CTE traversing a real hierarchy in AdventureWorks2012.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a view vw_CustomerOrderSummary joining Customer, Person, and SalesOrderHeader to show each customer's order count and total spend, then query it like a table; check sys.indexes to decide whether an indexed view would suit this case.
slots.deliverable: A working CREATE VIEW statement, a SELECT against that view, and a written note on indexed-view suitability.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a PIVOT query turning Sales.SalesOrderHeader order counts by TerritoryID into columns with order years as rows, then write an UNPIVOT query reshaping that result back into tall/normalized form, confirming the row count matches the original.
slots.deliverable: A working PIVOT cross-tab query and a matching UNPIVOT query reversing it back to normalized rows.

slots.practicalActivity: Solve the same business question — 'which customers have above-average total spend' — three ways: a correlated subquery, a CTE, and a view, comparing their readability in a short written note.
slots.deliverable: Three functionally-equivalent queries (subquery, CTE, view-based) answering the same question, with a comparison note.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Subqueries, CTEs, and Views: build one query that uses a CTE to pre-aggregate order totals per customer, uses EXISTS against that CTE to filter to customers above a threshold, then PIVOTs the result by order year.
slots.deliverable: One original multi-technique query chaining a CTE, an EXISTS filter, and a PIVOT, successfully executed in SSMS.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a script that DECLAREs 3 variables (INT, VARCHAR, DATETIME), assigns values with SELECT/SET, and PRINTs a formatted message using them; split it into 2 batches with GO and confirm the variables don't persist across the boundary.
slots.deliverable: A script demonstrating variable declaration and use, plus proof that GO resets variable scope.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a script that stores a real Production.Product.ListPrice in a variable and uses IF/ELSE with BEGIN/END blocks to PRINT different messages for 'budget', 'mid-range', and 'premium' price tiers.
slots.deliverable: A working IF/ELSE/BEGIN/END script that branches based on a real queried value.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a WHILE loop printing numbers 1-10 with a running total, then a cursor that iterates over the top 5 highest-priced products in Production.Product and PRINTs each product's name and price one row at a time.
slots.deliverable: A working WHILE loop script and a working cursor script that iterates real product rows.

slots.practicalActivity: Create usp_GetCustomerOrders taking a @CustomerID parameter, returning that customer's orders from Sales.SalesOrderHeader, with a default parameter value and an OUTPUT parameter returning the order count; EXEC it with 2 different customer IDs.
slots.deliverable: A working CREATE PROCEDURE with input and OUTPUT parameters, executed successfully with 2 different inputs.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a parameterized sp_executesql script that builds a SELECT whose filter column's value comes from a variable (not string concatenation); then create a small staging temp table with changed and new product rows and write a MERGE statement syncing it into a scratch copy of Production.Product.
slots.deliverable: One working sp_executesql script with parameterized dynamic SQL, plus a working MERGE statement with before/after row counts noted.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Programming with T-SQL: build an original stored procedure accepting a @MinTotal parameter, using IF/ELSE to validate it, and returning orders above that total using proper BEGIN/END and parameter handling — EXEC it twice with different threshold values.
slots.deliverable: One original parameterized stored procedure combining variables, IF/ELSE, and BEGIN/END, executed with 2 different parameter values.

slots.practicalActivity: On a scratch copy of a small table, write a script using BEGIN TRANSACTION, make an UPDATE, verify the change, then ROLLBACK and verify it reverted; repeat with COMMIT and verify it persists. Write one sentence per ACID property tying it to the demo.
slots.deliverable: A working transaction script demonstrating both ROLLBACK and COMMIT, plus 4 short written ACID explanations tied to the demo.

slots.practicalActivity: Open two SSMS query windows against the same scratch table: start an uncommitted UPDATE transaction in window 1, then attempt to SELECT/UPDATE the same rows in window 2 and observe the blocking; inspect the lock with sys.dm_tran_locks, then COMMIT window 1 and confirm window 2 unblocks.
slots.deliverable: A documented two-session blocking demo with notes on the lock type observed and how it resolved.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a TRY/CATCH block around an intentionally failing statement (e.g. an INSERT violating a constraint), capturing ERROR_MESSAGE/ERROR_NUMBER in the CATCH block; then write one RAISERROR and one THROW example raising a custom business-rule error.
slots.deliverable: A working TRY/CATCH script that captures a real error, plus one RAISERROR and one THROW example.

slots.practicalActivity: In SSMS's connection dialog, examine Windows Authentication vs. SQL Server Authentication; query sys.server_principals to list login accounts and their authentication type on your instance, then write a short recommendation for when you'd choose each mode.
slots.deliverable: A query result listing server logins by auth type, plus a short written recommendation for a given deployment scenario.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Transactions and Error Handling: write one script combining a transaction, TRY/CATCH, and THROW — attempt an UPDATE inside BEGIN TRANSACTION, deliberately trigger a constraint violation, catch it, ROLLBACK inside the CATCH block, and THROW a custom re-raised error.
slots.deliverable: One original script combining transactions, TRY/CATCH, ROLLBACK, and THROW into a safe error-handling pattern.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a query using OVER(PARTITION BY Color) to show each Production.Product row alongside the average ListPrice for its own color, then a ROW_NUMBER() query numbering each customer's orders from most recent to oldest, partitioned by CustomerID.
slots.deliverable: A PARTITION BY aggregate-window query and a ROW_NUMBER() per-customer ordering query.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a query ranking products by ListPrice within each ProductSubcategoryID using RANK() and DENSE_RANK(), comparing tie handling; then write an NTILE(4) query splitting customers into spending quartiles based on total order value.
slots.deliverable: A side-by-side RANK vs. DENSE_RANK query showing tie behavior, plus an NTILE(4) quartile-assignment query.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Window and Ranking Functions: build an original 'top 3 products per category by sales' report using ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY category ORDER BY total sales descending inside a CTE, filtering WHERE rn <= 3 in the outer query.
slots.deliverable: One original top-N-per-group report query using a window function inside a CTE, correctly limited to the top 3 rows per category.

lessons.title: The Cartesian Product: What Happens When Joins Go Wrong

slots.practicalActivity: Write a baseline query against Sales.SalesOrderDetail and time it with SSMS's query execution time; then deliberately omit a JOIN's ON condition between two tables to produce an accidental Cartesian product, observe the exploded row count, and fix it.
slots.deliverable: A timed baseline query, plus a before/after pair showing an accidental Cartesian product and its corrected join.

lessons.title: Joins vs. Subqueries: Which Is Faster, and Why
EXISTS vs. IN vs. JOIN for Existence Checks

slots.practicalActivity: Write 'customers with at least one order over $5,000' three ways — a JOIN with DISTINCT, an IN subquery, and an EXISTS subquery — then turn on Include Actual Execution Plan and compare the plans and relative costs.
slots.deliverable: Three functionally-equivalent queries (JOIN, IN, EXISTS) with execution-plan cost notes comparing them.

lessons.title: Clustered vs. Nonclustered Indexes: Choosing Wisely

slots.practicalActivity: Write a non-SARGable query (WHERE YEAR(OrderDate) = 2013) and a SARGable rewrite (WHERE OrderDate >= '2013-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2014-01-01') against Sales.SalesOrderHeader, comparing execution plans; then use Object Explorer to list that table's clustered and nonclustered indexes.
slots.deliverable: A non-SARGable/SARGable query pair with plan comparison, plus a written list of the table's clustered and nonclustered indexes.

lessons.title: Reading Execution Plans: Scans vs. Seeks

slots.practicalActivity: Create a filtered index on Sales.SalesOrderHeader for a narrow condition (e.g. WHERE Status = 5) with an included column, then write a query that benefits from it and confirm via the execution plan that it's an Index Seek rather than a full scan.
slots.deliverable: A CREATE INDEX statement (filtered, with INCLUDE), plus execution-plan notes confirming an Index Seek on it.

lessons.title: SET STATISTICS TIME and IO in Practice

slots.practicalActivity: Turn on SET STATISTICS TIME ON and SET STATISTICS IO ON, run 2 versions of the same query (one index-aided, one forced to scan), comparing CPU time and logical reads; then capture the XML execution plan for one of them.
slots.deliverable: Before/after STATISTICS TIME/IO output comparing two query versions, plus one captured XML execution plan.

lessons.title: Temp Tables vs. Table Variables vs. CTEs: Performance Tradeoffs

slots.practicalActivity: Solve the same multi-step aggregation problem three ways — a #temp table, a table variable, and a CTE — comparing execution plans; then find and fix 3 performance anti-patterns in earlier queries you wrote (SELECT *, non-SARGable WHERE, a scalar function on a filtered column).
slots.deliverable: Three equivalent query solutions with performance notes, plus 3 before/after anti-pattern rewrites with plan or STATISTICS IO evidence of improvement.

slots.practicalActivity: Take your Chapter 3 five-table join lab query, run it with Actual Execution Plan on, identify the most expensive operator, and rewrite the query to reduce its cost, documenting the specific change and before/after cost percentages.
slots.deliverable: One documented query optimization: original query, its most expensive plan operator, the rewritten query, and a before/after cost comparison.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab for Performance Tuning: pick 2 queries from earlier chapters and apply the full tuning checklist to each — SARGability, index usage, anti-patterns, and a temp-table/CTE comparison — writing a short tuning report for each with a final optimization recommendation.
slots.deliverable: A short written tuning report for 2 prior queries, each covering SARGability, index usage, and a final optimization recommendation.

slots.practicalActivity: On a scratch copy of 2 related AdventureWorks2012 tables, write CREATE TABLE statements defining a PRIMARY KEY on one and a FOREIGN KEY referencing it on the other, then prove the constraint by attempting (and catching) an INSERT with an invalid foreign-key value.
slots.deliverable: Two CREATE TABLE statements with a working PK/FK relationship, plus a failed INSERT showing the FK constraint being enforced.

slots.practicalActivity: On your scratch table, add a UNIQUE constraint on a column like an email or product code, and a CHECK constraint enforcing a business rule (e.g. ListPrice >= 0); test both by attempting inserts that should fail and succeed.
slots.deliverable: Working UNIQUE and CHECK constraints, each demonstrated with one failing and one passing INSERT.

slots.practicalActivity: Identify one real one-to-one relationship (e.g. Person.Person to HumanResources.Employee) and one real one-to-many relationship (e.g. Sales.Customer to Sales.SalesOrderHeader) in AdventureWorks2012 using Object Explorer's key diagrams, and write a short explanation of how each relationship is enforced.
slots.deliverable: A written identification of one real one-to-one and one real one-to-many relationship in AdventureWorks2012, with the enforcing keys named.

slots.practicalActivity: Find the many-to-many relationship between Production.Product and Purchasing.Vendor via the Purchasing.ProductVendor junction table and diagram it; then write a short before/after example showing a table violating 1NF (a column holding comma-separated values) and its corrected 1NF version.
slots.deliverable: A diagram of the Product-Vendor many-to-many relationship via its junction table, plus a before/after 1NF correction example.

slots.practicalActivity: Design a small denormalized sample table on paper (e.g. an order table repeating customer address per row) and normalize it step by step into 2NF then 3NF, writing the resulting CREATE TABLE statements; then query sys.databases to confirm the master, msdb, tempdb, and model system databases exist on your instance.
slots.deliverable: A documented 2NF/3NF normalization walkthrough with final CREATE TABLE statements, plus a sys.databases query confirming the 4 system databases.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a #local temp table in one session and confirm it's invisible from a second session, then create a ##global temp table and confirm the second session can see it; separately, open SQL Server Profiler (or its replacement, Extended Events) and capture a trace of one of your earlier SELECT queries running.
slots.deliverable: A documented local-vs-global temp table visibility test across two sessions, plus a captured trace of a real query.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending practice for Database Design Fundamentals: design and CREATE a brand-new 3-table mini-schema from scratch (e.g. a simple Orders/OrderItems/Products set) with proper primary keys, foreign keys, a UNIQUE constraint, and a CHECK constraint, normalized to at least 3NF.
slots.deliverable: A new 3-table CREATE TABLE schema with PK, FK, UNIQUE, and CHECK constraints, confirmed to be in 3NF.

slots.practicalActivity: Review your Chapter 11 mini-schema against a checklist: does every table have a primary key, does every relationship have an enforced foreign key, is there a redundant/repeating column that violates 1NF? Write a short remediation note for any issue found.
slots.deliverable: A written design-review checklist applied to your own mini-schema, with remediation notes for any issues found.

lessons.title: OLTP vs. OLAP: Two Different Worlds

slots.practicalActivity: Classify AdventureWorks2012 (the OLTP sales system) against AdventureWorksDW2014 (the OLAP data warehouse) by browsing both databases' Object Explorer trees and writing down 3 concrete structural differences you observe (table naming, normalization level, row counts).
slots.deliverable: A written OLTP-vs-OLAP comparison listing 3 concrete structural differences observed between AdventureWorks2012 and AdventureWorksDW2014.

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch (on paper or in a diagram tool) a data mart that a Sales department might carve out of AdventureWorksDW2014 containing only sales-relevant fact and dimension tables, and write a short note contrasting it with how a data lake would instead store AdventureWorks2012's raw export files.
slots.deliverable: A sketched Sales data-mart scope diagram plus a written data-mart-vs-data-lake contrast note.

lessons.title: Data Warehouse vs. Data Lake vs. Data Mart

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-paragraph decision memo choosing a warehouse, lake, or mart for a given fictional business need; then write out, step by step, how you'd move Sales.SalesOrderHeader data from AdventureWorks2012 into AdventureWorksDW2014's FactInternetSales as an ETL process vs. an ELT process.
slots.deliverable: A written warehouse/lake/mart decision memo, plus a step-by-step ETL vs. ELT process comparison for a real table migration.

slots.practicalActivity: In AdventureWorksDW2014, open FactInternetSales and identify 3 of its dimension tables (e.g. DimProduct, DimCustomer, DimDate) via the foreign keys in Object Explorer, then diagram the resulting star schema with the fact table in the center.
slots.deliverable: A star-schema diagram of FactInternetSales and 3 real connected dimension tables from AdventureWorksDW2014.

slots.practicalActivity: Find a normalized dimension chain in AdventureWorksDW2014 (e.g. DimProduct -> DimProductSubcategory -> DimProductCategory) and diagram it as a snowflake schema; then query DimCustomer or DimProduct for any Start/End date or current-flag columns and write a note on which SCD type they implement.
slots.deliverable: A snowflake-schema diagram of a real normalized dimension chain, plus a written identification of an SCD pattern in AdventureWorksDW2014.

lessons.title: Where T-SQL Fits in the BI/Warehousing Pipeline

slots.practicalActivity: Compare DimProduct's surrogate ProductKey against Production.Product's natural ProductID in AdventureWorks2012/DW2014 and write a short note on why the warehouse uses a surrogate key instead; then diagram the full pipeline from AdventureWorks2012 OLTP data through T-SQL ETL into AdventureWorksDW2014 and finally into a BI report.
slots.deliverable: A surrogate-vs-natural key comparison note, plus an end-to-end OLTP-to-ETL-to-warehouse-to-BI pipeline diagram naming the real databases involved.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending review for Data Warehouse Concepts: write a T-SQL SELECT against AdventureWorksDW2014 that joins FactInternetSales to DimDate and DimProduct to produce 'total sales by year and product category' — a real star-schema query using everything in this chapter.
slots.deliverable: One working star-schema query against AdventureWorksDW2014 joining a fact table to at least 2 dimension tables for a real reporting question.

slots.practicalActivity: Course-closing capstone lab: write an original end-to-end T-SQL script that stages a small extract from AdventureWorks2012 (via a temp table or CTE), transforms it with CASE/date functions, and inserts the result into a scratch star-schema-style fact/dimension pair you design yourself — combining joins, aggregation, data-type handling, and warehouse concepts from across the whole course.
slots.deliverable: One original end-to-end T-SQL capstone script that extracts, transforms, and loads AdventureWorks2012 data into a self-designed scratch fact/dimension pair.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can write real T-SQL against SQL Server end to end — querying, filtering, joining, aggregating, and manipulating strings and dates; building subqueries, CTEs, views, stored procedures, and transactions with proper error handling; using window functions and reading execution plans to tune performance; and designing a normalized OLTP schema alongside a star-schema data warehouse, which is the exact SQL foundation a BI Engineer builds every downstream report and model on.
